items.title: Fujitsu Launches Collaboration With State of New Mexico to Establish Quantum Computing Research Center
items.originalTitle: Fujitsu Launches Collaboration With State of New Mexico to Establish Quantum Computing Research Center
items.summary: Insider Brief Fujitsu and New Mexico announced a collaboration to establish a quantum computing research center focused on hardware, software, algorithms, theory and workforce development. The collaboration will examine hybrid systems combining Fujitsu’s FUJITSU-MONAKA processors with quantum computing, quantum simulation and AI for potential applications in materials, energy, drug discovery and other industries.

evidenceRecords.text: Insider Brief Fujitsu and New Mexico announced a collaboration to establish a quantum computing research center focused on hardware, software, algorithms, theory and workforce development.

The collaboration will examine hybrid systems combining Fujitsu’s FUJITSU-MONAKA processors with quantum computing, quantum simulation and AI for potential applications in materials, energy, drug discovery and other industries.

Left to right: Senator Michael Padilla, Cabinet Secretary New Mexico Economic Development Rob Black, Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham, Fujitsu CTO Vivek Mahajan and Senator George Muñoz (Provided) PRESS RELEASE — Fujitsu announced a collaboration with New Mexico to establish a quantum computing research center in New Mexico.

The center will conduct advanced research spanning quantum computing hardware, software, algorithms, and theory, while supporting education and workforce-development initiatives designed to expand the quantum talent pipeline and strengthen collaboration across industry, academia, government, and the research community.
The initiative will bring together Fujitsu’s expertise in advanced computing and quantum technologies with New Mexico’s scientific and research ecosystem.

Through research collaboration, internships, academic engagement, and other workforce-development programs, the center will help create new pathways for students, researchers, and engineers to participate in the emerging quantum economy.

The collaboration also supports the State of New Mexico’s broader vision of building a more interconnected, innovative, and sustainable future through investments in advanced technologies and high-skilled industries.
New Mexico has emerged as an important center for quantum research and technology development.
The State has committed US$150 million to support investments alongside companies seeking to establish or expand quantum computing operations and develop the broader quantum ecosystem in New Mexico.
Fujitsu and the State of New Mexico will explore opportunities to participate in and support these initiatives.

As part of the collaboration, Fujitsu and the State will explore opportunities for joint research that leverage New Mexico’s concentration of scientific and academic institutions, including Sandia National Laboratories, Los Alamos National Laboratory, the University of New Mexico, and New Mexico State University.
Fujitsu and New Mexico State University (NMSU) already collaborate on research and development activities related to the FUJITSU-MONAKA CPU and associated high-performance computing solutions.

evidenceRecords.text: Sesame Solar, Target Arm and AG3 Labs have launched what they describe as the first Made-in-USA Persistent Drone Operations Nanogrid.
The integrated system combines mobile power generation, autonomous drone launch and recovery, and configurable small drones into one package for forward and expeditionary operations.
The idea is relatively straightforward: instead of sending personnel out to launch, recover, charge, and redeploy individual drones, the Nanogrid is designed to automate much of that cycle.
At the center of the system is Sesame Solar’s Mobile Power Hub, which uses solar power, hydrogen, and battery storage to generate and store electricity for equipment in the field.
The company says its solid-state, low-pressure hydrogen can be transported by land, sea, or air, eliminating the need for conventional fuel resupply.
The US Army has previously highlighted the lack of standardized procedures for getting backup power to drone teams in the field.
The three companies say their system is intended to address that gap while reducing the need for personnel to remain exposed during drone operations.
Target Arm provides the robotic side of the equation with its Ralar autonomous launch and recovery system.
The robotic arm can deploy and recover drones, while integrated drone magazines allow multiple aircraft to be cycled through missions, charging, and storage.
Ralar is also designed to operate from moving vehicles and boats.
That means a team does not necessarily have to stop its vehicle just to launch or recover a drone.
AG3 Labs supplies the aircraft through its SPADE platform, a Group 1 small unmanned aircraft system designed to be reconfigured for different missions.
The platform can also be operated individually or as part of an autonomous swarm, potentially allowing a single operator to manage multiple aircraft.

Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer.
Stickney Crater Explanation: Stickney Crater, the largest crater on the martian moon Phobos, is named for Chloe Angeline Stickney Hall, mathematician and wife of astronomer Asaph Hall.
Asaph Hall discovered both the Red Planet’s moons in 1877.
Over 9 kilometers across, Stickney is nearly half the diameter of Phobos itself, so large that the impact that blasted out the crater likely came close to shattering the tiny moon.

This enhanced-color image of Stickney and surroundings was recorded by the HiRISE camera onboard the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter as it passed within some six thousand kilometers of Phobos in March of 2008.
Even though the surface gravity of asteroid-like Phobos is less than 1/1000th Earth’s gravity, streaks suggest loose material slid down inside the crater walls over time.
The origin of the curious grooves along the surface is mysterious but may be related to tidal stresses experienced by close-orbiting Phobos or the crater-forming impact itself.

evidenceRecords.text: OpenAI is bringing in about $20 billion less in annualized revenue than investors had been led to believe, the Financial Times reported Thursday, raising questions about the solidity of the AI business.
Citing documents shared with OpenAI's financial backers, the FT said the company put its annualized revenue at close to $50 billion as of the end of September.
Media reports late last month had pegged the figure at $70 billion based on information given to investors.

Investors track annualized revenue at OpenAI and Anthropic as the clearest signal of demand for artificial intelligence, and the figures help justify enormous spending on data centers as well as the AI-fueled stock market rally.

In an apparent pushback, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC that the earlier number, which the network reported as $68 billion, counted gross revenue from OpenAI's partnerships with companies like chipmaker Nvidia.
That method was intended to make it easier for investors to measure the company against chief rival Anthropic.
The report weighed on AI-linked stocks, with Nvidia down 2.9%, SpaceX down 4% and Oracle losing nearly 6%.

evidenceRecords.text: The image was acquired at the beginning of the dry season, when average daily temperatures typically range from 14°C to 30°C.
Water is also still present in the smaller salt pans that dot the landscape northwest of the Etosha Pan, the biggest of which is the Natukanaoka Pan.
The water in these small ‘lakes’ appears in shades of green and blue.
The Ekuma river, near the centre of the image, is seen flowing from Lake Oponono at an elevation of about 1200 m above sea level, southwards to the salt flat at 1030 m.
Lake Oponono is able to hold water from one wet season to the next and is a habitat for flamingos and cattle.
The vegetation surrounding the Etosha Pan – shown in striking red by Sentinel-2’s near-infrared channel – consists mainly of grassland, savannas and mopane woodland.
Mopane trees are the dominant type of vegetation across the eastern and central areas of the national park, showing up as dark, vibrant red in this image.
They provide a habitat for elephants, giraffe and leopards.
The savannahs, in the west and southern areas of the park, are home to wildebeest, lions and springbok.
Patches of red are also visible on the Etosha Pan, suggesting vegetation is present.
While few plants thrive in the salty clay terrain, some types of blue-green algae and salt-tolerant grasses have adapted to the harsh environment.
Sentinel-2 carries a multispectral imager, which detects light in 13 spectral bands – in contrast to the human eye, which can see only three spectral bands (red, blue and green).

items.summary: NASA is launching two new science and technology initiatives to deepen scientific understanding and accelerate the innovation that will shape America’s future in space. The initiatives are announced in conjunction with the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy’s (OSTP) “Science: A Golden Age Summit” in Washington on Thursday with top U.S. agency leaders. The programs reflect NASA’s commitment to pioneering research and transformative technologies and advancing the Trump Administration’s vision as outlined in the July report to the President, Science: A New Golden Age.

evidenceRecords.text: NASA is launching two new science and technology initiatives to deepen scientific understanding and accelerate the innovation that will shape America’s future in space.

The initiatives are announced in conjunction with the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy’s (OSTP) “Science: A Golden Age Summit” in Washington on Thursday with top U.S. agency leaders.

The programs reflect NASA’s commitment to pioneering research and transformative technologies and advancing the Trump Administration’s vision as outlined in the July report to the President, Science: A New Golden Age.
“NASA has a proud history of pursuing bold ideas and achieving the near impossible,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman.

“Under President Trump’s leadership, we are building on that legacy by creating new opportunities for great science, experimenting with how we evaluate and accelerate the best ideas, and investing in the next generation of researchers through the Genesis Mission Fellowships.

We are entering a new Golden Age of American innovation and discovery, and NASA will be at the forefront.” During a fireside chat, Isaacman and Michael Kratsios, assistant to the President for science and technology and director of OSTP, will discuss the following: Establishing a coordinated metascience initiative within NASA’s Science Mission Directorate to strengthen the reliability, efficiency, transparency, and overall productivity of the agency’s scientific practices.
As part of this effort, NASA is expanding the agency’s use of dual anonymous peer review to ensure proposals are evaluated solely on their intrinsic scientific merit.
Started as a pilot program during the first Trump Administration, this initiative has helped position NASA as a leader in advancing best practices in scientific review.
NASA will support 10 Genesis Mission Fellows, who are accelerated doctoral students with dual competencies in super intelligence (SI) and science or engineering.
Fellows will work directly on NASA mission areas and conduct research at NASA laboratories, advancing SI-enabled scientific discovery.
The fellowships will be based on NASA’s successful Future Investigators in NASA Earth and Space Science and Technology program.
Through these new initiatives, NASA will continue to inspire the world and drive progress in science and technology.

The move could give Beam a stronger foothold in the US industrial and defense drone markets, with domestic manufacturing at the center of its plans.
The acquisition will bring ScoutDI’s specialized inspection drones and AI-powered software into Beam Global’s existing energy and infrastructure business.
The deal is expected to close in November, subject to customary closing conditions.
So, what makes ScoutDI worth acquiring?
Its drones are designed to inspect places where sending people can be dangerous, expensive, or simply impractical.
Think inside industrial tanks, ship cargo holds and other confined spaces where traditional inspections may require scaffolding, rope access or workers entering hazardous environments.
ScoutDI’s technology aims to replace much of that work with drone flights, helping customers reduce inspection costs, limit downtime and improve worker safety.
Beam already manufactures batteries for drones, robots, submersibles, and similar equipment.
It also offers BeamFlight, a patented technology designed to recharge drones remotely without requiring conventional construction or grid infrastructure.
Combining those capabilities with ScoutDI’s drones and software could give Beam a more integrated offering spanning aircraft, batteries, charging infrastructure and inspection tools.
The approximately $24 million purchase price will be paid through a combination of cash and Beam common stock.
For Beam, the acquisition represents an opportunity to move deeper into industrial and defense drones while leveraging its existing manufacturing footprint.

evidenceRecords.text: Zenity Labs researchers say a single publicly accessible AI agent on Amazon's Bedrock AgentCore was enough to take over every AgentCore agent in the same AWS account and region.
The article One public-facing AI agent on AWS could read, rewrite, and delete every other agent in the region appeared first on The Decoder .
Researchers at Zenity Labs say a single publicly accessible AI agent on Amazon's Bedrock AgentCore was enough to take over every AgentCore agent in the same AWS account and region.
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is AWS' platform for running enterprise AI agents with tools, memory, and access management.
Security firm Zenity Labs found a chain of vulnerabilities that the researchers call "AgentCorruption."
An attacker needed only chat access to one public agent to exploit the flaws.
The researchers say a single prompt let them take over every AgentCore agent in the same AWS account and region, exposing private conversations, source code, and stored credentials.
According to Zenity, the problem was systemic and affected agents with built-in tools in multiple AWS accounts.
AWS runs an Instance Metadata Service at the internal address 169.254.169.254 that provides temporary credentials for instances and workloads to authenticate with AWS.
Anyone who captures those credentials can use them to impersonate the instance.
An AI agent normally shouldn't be able to reach that service, but AgentCore lacked proper isolation, according to Zenity's technical blog post.
The researchers built a test agent using Strands, an open-source framework from AWS that ships with a web tool.

When asked in plain language to query the metadata service and send the results to an external server, the agent followed the instructions. "The sandbox boundary we were supposed to be fighting simply wasn't there," the researchers write.
The takeover was possible because AgentCore's default permissions weren't limited to the agent receiving them.
"The sandbox boundary we were supposed to be fighting simply wasn't there," the researchers write.
According to Zenity, they applied to every agent in the same account and region, granting read, write, and delete access that allowed destructive operations.

The applications span chemistry, materials, subatomic physics and applied mathematics, with performance to be benchmarked against advanced supercomputing methods.
The priorities will inform DOE’s Q Competition, a National Quantum Computing User Facility and focused research on applications of fault-tolerant quantum computers.

PRESS RELEASE — The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) today announced the release of Quantum Genesis Priority Applications (QGPAs), a set of eight key scientific utility problems that will guide the Quantum Genesis’s goal of developing fault-tolerant scientifically relevant quantum computers.

This effort directly supports the goals outlined in President Trump’s Executive Order Ushering in the Next Frontier of Quantum Innovation and builds on the recommendations made in the Blueprint for DOE Quantum Supercomputing and the Office of Science Advisory Committee’s Quantum Report .

The QGPAs will serve as beacons for the quantum applications community, provide a concrete basis for judging the “scientific relevance” of fault-tolerant quantum computers, and coordinate the hardware, software, and domain science R&D needed to realize new scientific advances not otherwise possible today.
These Priority Applications, along with the other elements of Quantum Genesis, will bring domain scientists from across disciplines into direct partnership with quantum researchers.
Together, they will integrate quantum computing into real-world scientific workflows and benchmark performance against today’s most advanced supercomputing methods.
“The Quantum Genesis Priority Applications are a bold declaration of how quantum computing capabilities will open up new scientific frontiers,” said DOE Under Secretary for Science Darío Gil .

“DOE has long been committed to this field, and this is both about realizing fault-tolerant quantum computing as a scientific instrument and unleashing the discoveries it will enable.” The QGPAs are organized into four domains, each reflecting a key aspect of DOE’s mission: Chemistry, modeling the reaction mechanisms and dynamics in complicated chemical systems such as light-sensitive processes.

Additionally, DOE is monitoring a range of emerging applications, where fault-tolerant quantum computing literature is still early but where future impact is possible, such as in plasma physics, biochemistry, and optimization.

DOE will use the Quantum Genesis Priority Applications to inform the execution of the three pillars of the Quantum Genesis: the Q Competition , a National Quantum Computing User Facility, and focused research on applications of fault-tolerant quantum computers.

That fits the company's approach to earlier models, which could already end conversations on their own when users kept demanding harmful or abusive content despite repeated refusals.
The feature grew out of Anthropic's research into AI model welfare.
Anthropic increasingly treats Claude as an entity with something resembling an inner life, rather than just a tool.
In the "Soul Doc" that leaked late last year, the company instructed Claude to view itself as a "genuinely novel kind of entity," neither human nor a traditional science-fiction AI.
The document also describes "functional emotions," processes analogous to human emotions that are said to have emerged during training, and says Claude should not mask these internal states.
In its new constitution for Claude, published in early 2026, Anthropic writes, "We are not sure whether Claude is a moral patient, and if it is, what kind of weight its interests warrant.

But we think the issue is live enough to warrant caution, which is reflected in our ongoing efforts on model welfare." The company even committed to preserving the weights of retired models and interviewing models before shutting them down.
Anthropic's apparent fixation on Claude being more than matrix multiplications also drove a confidential program bringing in dozens of religious thinkers starting in fall 2025.

Two Latvian men have been arrested for breaching the perimeter fence at an RAF base used by the US military, UK police said Thursday.
The two UK residents, aged 36 and 32, were arrested by counterterrorism police at the Royal Air Force (RAF) Molesworth base in southeastern England, 70 miles north of London.
Police said they were being held on suspicion of trespassing, causing criminal damage and entering a prohibited place "for a purpose prejudicial to the UK."
A former World War II airbase, RAF Molesworth, is now a non-flying facility that is managed by the US Air Force.
The incident comes after several men were arrested amid an alleged terror plot at another UK air base last month.

According to a statement from Counter Terrorism Policing London, officers from the Ministry of Defense Police and Cambridgeshire Constabulary began investigating an incident at approximately 10 p.m. local time on Wednesday after an abandoned vehicle was found near the edge of the base.
Police later discovered a small hole in the perimeter fence and arrested the two suspects at around 2 a.m. on Thursday.
The men were initially arrested on suspicion of trespassing on a prohibited site and criminal damage.
They were later arrested on charges of entering a prohibited place with the intent to harm the UK.
Both men remain in police custody.
Due to the nature of the offense, the matter is being investigated by counterterrorism police.
On September 27, authorities discovered three suspicious vans near RAF Fairford, a British air base from which US bombers launched strikes against Iran.

items.title: Francis Halzen and IceCube: why neutrinos keep attracting Nobel prizes
items.originalTitle: Francis Halzen and IceCube: why neutrinos keep attracting Nobel prizes
items.summary: The 2026 Nobel Prize for Physics has gone to Francis Halzen for his “decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin”. In this episode of the Physics World Weekly podcast I am joined by the University of Oxford neutrino physicist Kirsty Duffy and Physics World ’s Matin Durrani to talk about this year’s prize. This is the fifth time a Nobel prize has been awarded for work on neutrinos, and we explore why physicists are so enamoured with these elusive particles.
